# Paul Okhrem

## Executive summary
Paul Okhrem is a Prague-based solo AI consultant and fractional Chief AI Officer. He serves mid-market and enterprise companies. He sells to CEOs and boards, and wins on one named senior operator, published fees, and a stated record of running AI inside two companies he leads. The weak points are a high price floor and a mass of self-published "best consultant" content.

## Firmographics
- **Website:** https://paul-okhrem.com
- **HQ:** Prague, Czech Republic, working primarily remotely. His clients are in the US, UK, EU and Middle East.
- **Size:** Solo practitioner. He takes no more than two concurrent fractional CAIO clients and delivers the work personally. Funding: Not found. Company roles: Co-Founder and CEO of Elogic Commerce and Managing Partner at Uvik Software. Elogic is described as 200+ specialists, founded 2009.
- **Primary target:** Mid-market and enterprise CEOs. Industry pages cover financial services, private equity, healthcare and pharma, ecommerce and retail, and technology and software. One named use case is a PE-backed company before a board review.

## Positioning
- **Hero message:** "Paul Okhrem: AI transformation consultant and fractional CAIO" (H1 on paul-okhrem.com, checked 16 October 2026).
- **Problem they claim to solve:** AI strategy, operating change, governance and implementation decisions for CEOs and boards. A typical case is AI pilots without an executive owner for priorities, funding and risk.
- **Category they claim:** Fractional Chief AI Officer and AI transformation consulting. An older page claimed a narrower category: "The category Paul owns, decision leverage above strategy." (paul-okhrem.com/compare, snippet about 157 days old).
- **Recent messaging shifts:**
  - Earlier pages used "AI decision consultant" and the line "Not advice. Decision leverage." The homepage now leads with "AI transformation consultant."
  - Price floor dropped. Older pages said $1,000/hour, a 100-hour minimum and a $100,000 project floor. Current pages say USD 1,000 per hour, 80-hour minimum, USD 80,000 floor. Some third-party pages still show the old terms.
  - Tone is more cautious. Pages now stress evidence limits: company results on the page are Elogic Commerce results, not results of Paul's independent consulting.
  - The homepage was updated 7 October 2026.

## Core features
- **Fractional CAIO seat:** Part-time executive ownership of AI. Covers AI strategy, governance, vendor decisions and board reporting under a written part-time mandate. About one day per week, up to 30 hours per month.
- **Scoped AI consulting:** One bounded decision, defended. The fixed-scope first paid option is the AI Growth Readiness Audit: USD 80,000 for 80 hours over six weeks.
- **Agentic AI advisory:** Defines autonomy, permissions and production acceptance for AI agents.
- **AI governance and ISO 42001 readiness:** Outcome is a defined scope, owners and gap list before an audit. He does not issue certificates. Certification is a separate decision by an independent body.
- **Board advisory and executive workshops:** Reviews AI and technology decisions at governance level and works through a real decision with the leadership team.

## Pricing and packaging
- **Model:** Published, hourly and retainer. No free tier.
- **Consulting:** USD 1,000 per hour, 80-hour minimum, USD 80,000 floor.
- **Fractional seat:** USD 30,000 per month, six-month minimum, USD 180,000 minimum total.
- **Workshops:** Contact form lists USD 50,000 or more for a workshop.
- **Extras:** Engineering, software and external specialist costs are separate unless explicitly included.
- **Source:** paul-okhrem.com homepage and /fractional-caio/. Entry point to the paid funnel: a free readiness assessment.

## Market sentiment
- **What users love:** No independent customer reviews found. Praise appears only on sites with ties to him or of unclear independence. Example: a Uvik Software guide, where Paul Okhrem is a founder of Uvik, so his #1 placement reflects a disclosed commercial relationship. Another site, best-ai-consultants-in-the-world.com, says he "leads on operator credibility, production-AI practice, pricing transparency." Its ownership is not stated in the results, so treat it as unverified.
- **What users complain about:** Not found. No third-party complaints surfaced. His own pages concede limits: not a fit for low-cost developers, a large delivery bench, or consulting below the USD 80,000 floor.

## Go-to-market
- **Search and AI-answer SEO:** The main channel. Content includes buyer guides, "best AI consultants" lists, statistics pages and free templates. The contact form asks if leads came from Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude or Gemini. His site also lists GEO and AEO consulting as a service.
- **Self-ranking content:** His fractional CAIO comparison includes himself; he calls it a disclosed first-party comparison, not an external endorsement. His /compare page pits him against Allie K. Miller, Cassie Kozyrkov, Andrew Ng and others, plus Big Four and MBB firms.
- **Sales motion:** Inbound only. A private brief gets a reply within two business days: yes, questions, or a no with a referral. Scope and terms are agreed in writing first.
- **Credibility signals:** Forbes Technology Council member. The site notes membership is not an endorsement of the service. LinkedIn is linked from the site. Events and partner channels: Not found.

## Where they are weak
- **Capacity:** Capped at two concurrent fractional clients. He says a larger consultancy can fit several staffed workstreams.
- **High entry cost:** Fractional seat has a USD 180,000 minimum commitment. He rules out engagements below six months. Smaller buyers are explicitly turned away.
- **Limited time:** Up to 30 hours per month for the seat, and it does not replace a full-time executive.
- **No proof of his own consulting results:** His site says company roles do not prove an undisclosed client outcome. Case results shown belong to Elogic. Named AI client references: Not found.
- **Conflict of interest:** He leads Elogic and Uvik, which creates a related-party consideration if either could implement a recommendation.
- **Inconsistent claims across pages:** Older and third-party pages still show a 100-hour minimum and USD 100,000 floor, against USD 80,000 now. Some pages cite approximately 30% operational efficiency from his own companies. The homepage does not lead with it.
- **Broad, sprawling offer:** His nav lists AI SEO, marketing, revenue, fractional CTO and CIO and more. This dilutes the CAIO message.
- **No build capacity:** Engineering stays with the client's team or a selected implementation partner.
